provenance.notes: Edu family batch. Recurring weekly lessons, low web sophistication, parents book at night. Ranges are planning figures, not quotes.

pageStructurePlus.contains: Piano, guitar, violin, drums, voice and ukulele compared by starting age, hand size, practice noise, and whether to rent or buy the first instrument
pageStructurePlus.why: Parents of a six-year-old don't know whether to start piano or guitar. The music school that answers that question gets the first lesson.

pageStructurePlus.contains: Each music teacher's instruments and genres, classical, rock, jazz, worship or musical theatre, their teaching style, and which ages they teach best
pageStructurePlus.why: A teen who wants to play rock guitar won't stay with a classical teacher. Matching by genre is how studios keep students for years.

pageStructurePlus.contains: Seasonal piano and guitar recitals, student band showcases at local venues, what each student plays, dress, and how families invite grandparents
pageStructurePlus.why: Performing is why kids keep practising. Parents choose a music school that gives their child a stage, not just a lesson room.

pageStructurePlus.contains: Preparation for graded music exams, all-state and honour band auditions, college music school auditions, theory lessons and required repertoire
pageStructurePlus.why: Serious students and their parents look for a teacher with an audition track record and a plan. They pay more and book more weeks.

pageStructurePlus.contains: Hourly rehearsal rooms with backline, the recording booth, engineer rates, demo packages for students and local bands, and booking rules
pageStructurePlus.why: Studios with rooms earn from them at night. Local bands book rehearsal and recording time online or go elsewhere.

pageStructurePlus.contains: Lessons for adults returning to piano or picking up guitar for the first time, daytime and evening slots, and how a teacher paces adult learners
pageStructurePlus.why: Adults fill daytime lesson slots kids can't use, and they only book when the page says it's not too late to start.

designDirections.name: First Lesson
designDirections.bestFor: Solo music teachers and small studios that need a first-lesson booking and a clear rate
designDirections.headlineSample: Guitar and piano lessons in {City}. Book a first lesson.
designDirections.whyItFits: Cobalt and butter with a typewriter slab feel like a gig poster, which suits a rock and pop teacher, and the split hero keeps the booking button visible.

designDirections.name: Weekly Lesson
designDirections.bestFor: Music schools with several teachers, instruments by age and recitals each season
designDirections.headlineSample: Music lessons for {City} kids and adults
designDirections.whyItFits: The family combo. Sky Kite's rounded type is friendly to young beginners, and the card stack sorts lessons by instrument and teacher.

designDirections.name: Conservatory
designDirections.bestFor: Classical piano and strings studios preparing students for auditions and competitions
designDirections.headlineSample: Classical piano and strings instruction in {City}
designDirections.whyItFits: Gallery White's Didone display reads like a concert programme, and the clean white ground lets a grand piano photo carry the page.

openers.line: Your music studio's Google listing has a phone number but no website, so a parent searching piano lessons in {City} can't see teachers, rates or open lesson times.
openers.hook: Open their Maps listing and confirm there is no Website button. Screenshot it for when they reply.
openers.linkLine: Here's the music lesson page behind that button: {demo-link}

openers.line: The website link for the music school goes to Facebook, where the latest post about open guitar lesson slots is weeks down the page.
openers.hook: Tap the link and find the most recent openings or lesson post. Note its date.
openers.linkLine: Music lesson openings by instrument, on one page: {demo-link}

openers.line: The music school site on your listing names a teacher who seems to have moved on and a recital date from a past year. Parents notice details like that.
openers.hook: Open the site and find one stale detail: an old teacher, a past recital, old rates. Note it.
openers.linkLine: Same music school, current and bookable: {demo-link}

openers.line: I opened your music lessons site on my phone and the teacher list overlapped the menu. Parents look for a piano teacher on their phone after dinner.
openers.hook: Only if they have a site. Load it on your phone and note what breaks. Screenshot it for when they reply.
openers.linkLine: The same music school, rebuilt for a phone: {demo-link}

openers.line: Starting music lessons with you means leaving a voicemail while you're teaching. A first-lesson booking with the instrument and age would take that parent tonight.
openers.hook: Look for any trial or first lesson booking. If it's call or email only, the angle holds.
openers.linkLine: A first music lesson booking that works at night: {demo-link}

openers.line: Your clips of students playing their first full song are the best thing on the music school's page, and they're gone in a week. A recitals page would keep them working.
openers.hook: Find a recent student performance or recital post and note the piece or instrument.
openers.linkLine: Your students' performances, kept where parents look: {demo-link}

openers.line: Your reviews have parents saying their child finally practises piano without a fight. That review belongs right beside the first lesson button.
openers.hook: Read their reviews and copy one phrase about a teacher or practising. Quote it if they reply.
openers.linkLine: Music lesson reviews beside the booking: {demo-link}

openers.line: September and right after the holidays, when a guitar or keyboard was a gift, are when families start music lessons. The studio with open times online books them first.
openers.hook: Use this in August and late December. Name the moment: back to school or the gift under the tree.

openers.line: Parents decide on guitar lessons after dinner, once the kids beg again. Right now the music school can't show open times or take a booking at that hour.
openers.hook: Look for comments asking 'do you have openings' or 'what age can they start'. Note one.
openers.linkLine: A music lesson page that books at 9pm: {demo-link}

openers.line: Saw you're looking for a drum or voice teacher for the music school. Good teachers look at how the studio presents itself before they reply.
openers.hook: Only if they posted for teachers. Note the instrument.
openers.linkLine: A music school page with a teach-here section: {demo-link}

openers.line: You teach piano in students' homes, but nothing says whether you come to {Neighborhood}. Parents choosing in-home music lessons check that first.
openers.hook: Only if they mention in-home or travelling lessons. Check whether areas are listed.
openers.linkLine: An in-home music lesson page with your areas: {demo-link}

openers.line: I couldn't find a monthly or per-lesson rate for music lessons anywhere. Parents comparing piano teachers tend to call the one with a price on the page.
openers.hook: Check every page and post for rates. If none, the angle holds.
openers.linkLine: Music lesson rates by length, priced plainly: {demo-link}

openers.line: Your teachers' music degrees, orchestra seats and band credits are why a parent should choose the studio, and none of it shows where they'd look.
openers.hook: Look for teacher bios, degrees or performing credits in posts. Never invent one.
openers.linkLine: Your music teachers, their training and their gigs: {demo-link}

openers.line: It sounds like most new music students are siblings or friends of current ones. Their parents still look the studio up before the first lesson.
openers.hook: Look for reviews mentioning siblings or friends who also take lessons. Quote it.
openers.linkLine: Where a referred music parent would land: {demo-link}

openers.line: Watching {specific recent job} on your page, that's the clip I'd open the music school site with. It shows a parent exactly where weekly lessons lead.
openers.hook: Pick their newest performance, recital or student band post and name it exactly.
openers.linkLine: That student performance, front and centre: {demo-link}

sequence.dm1:
Hi {Owner} — that {specific recent job} you posted made me smile.

I looked for a site for {Business Name} and found the listing and your social pages, but no teachers, rates or open lesson times. I put together a sample music lesson page with instruments, teachers by genre and a first-lesson booking, with marked placeholders where your photos would go.

Would you like me to send it over?
sequence.dm2:
{Owner} — following up in case my message got lost between lessons. Here's the sample music school site for {Business Name}: {demo-link}

It has an instrument chooser, teachers by genre, a recitals page, audition prep and a first-lesson booking. If it's not for you, say so and I won't message again.
sequence.call:
"Hi, is this {Owner}? I'm {Your Name}, I build websites for music teachers and music schools here in {City}. I sent you a message a couple of days ago, did it come through?"

IF NO:
"Easy to miss when you're teaching back to back. Short version: I built a sample site for {Business Name} with instruments, teachers and a first-lesson booking, with marked placeholders where your photos would go. Can I email you the link?"

IF YES:
"What did you think?"
 → let them talk, don't fill the silence
"The build runs {Build Range}, then {Care Range} a month for hosting and teacher or rate changes. For a studio your size I'd normally quote about {Build Price}."
"Can I walk you through it for ten minutes before your first afternoon student?"

CLOSE:
"I'll send a one-page scope and a deposit invoice. We start the day it clears, and it's live before September sign-ups."

objections.objection: My students come from word of mouth.
objections.handler: "That means the teaching is good. The referred parent still looks you up, and a page with rates and open times turns that recommendation into a booked first lesson."

objections.objection: My lesson software has a sign-up page.
objections.handler: "Keep it for billing and the calendar. It can't help a parent choose piano or guitar, or show your teachers. The site explains, then sends them to the same sign-up."

objections.objection: I teach from home, I don't need a website.
objections.handler: "Home studios need it most. The site shows the room, the parking and your rules, so new families feel comfortable arriving at a house."

objections.objection: Summer is slow, I'll think about it in fall.
objections.handler: "Fall sign-ups start searching in August. Building in summer means the page is ranking when they look."

objections.objection: One of my students' parents made our site.
objections.handler: "Generous of them, keep them involved. I'll hand over the instrument chooser and booking. If updating teachers each term gets old, the offer stands."
"{Build Range}. For you about {Build Price}, because it's instruments, teachers and a first-lesson booking. A couple of new weekly students cover it within the year."

email.subject: Music lesson site for {Business Name}

sequence.voicemail: "Hi {Owner}, it's {Your Name}. I build websites for music schools in {City}, and I put together a sample one for {Business Name} with a first-lesson booking. I'll email you the link. {Your Phone}. Thanks."
sequence.takedown:
{Owner} — I'm taking the {Business Name} music lesson demo down on Friday to free up the space.

Want me to leave it up? One word is fine either way.
sequence.nurture:
Hi {Owner} — after the holidays, lots of new guitars and keyboards need a teacher. Thought of you.

The site is still here whenever you want it, and nothing's changed on price. {demo-link} if you want another look.

bullets: Peg the build to a couple of students' year of weekly lessons, never to the price of an instrument.
Price teacher pages by teacher count. A solo teacher needs one page, a school with many teachers needs a filterable directory.
The first-lesson booking with instrument and age questions is its own line and the main reason to buy.
Only quote rehearsal and recording rental for studios that actually have rooms and gear.
Keep monthly add-ons under one student's monthly tuition.
Sell in July for September starts and in early December for the post-holiday new-instrument wave.

lineItems.item: First-lesson booking with instrument and age
lineItems.description: Max with teacher matching by instrument, genre and age, a lesson length choice and reminder texts.
Max with many teachers, instrument and genre filters, a short clip per teacher and open-slot display.
Max with every instrument compared by age, plus rent-or-buy advice and links to a local music store.
Max with recital sign-up, piece submission, venue details and a past performances gallery.
Max with several rooms, hourly rates, engineer add-on, deposits and late-night access rules.

lineItems.item: Summer rock camp or music camp page
lineItems.description: Max with weekly camp sessions, band placement by level, a final show and registration.
Max when the booking, rates, instrument chooser and policies are all translated.

whatElseYouSell.name: Recital filming and teacher clips
whatElseYouSell.pitchLine: "Film the recital from a good angle and a short clip of each music teacher playing, so the site has sound and faces, students only with parent consent."
whatElseYouSell.when: At the next recital. Consent forms go home with the recital programme.

whatElseYouSell.name: Google profile upkeep for the music school
whatElseYouSell.pitchLine: "Open lesson times by instrument and recital dates posted to the music school's Google profile weekly, so piano and guitar searches nearby find a busy studio."

whatElseYouSell.name: Review asks after a first recital
whatElseYouSell.pitchLine: "The day after a student's first recital, proud parents get a short text asking them to review the music school."
whatElseYouSell.when: Set up before the next recital. The easiest second sale.

whatElseYouSell.name: Back-to-school and new-instrument lesson ads
whatElseYouSell.pitchLine: "Local ads for piano and guitar lessons in late August and right after the holidays, pointed at the first-lesson booking and paused when teachers fill."
whatElseYouSell.when: Pitch in July and early December. Ad spend is on top.

whatElseYouSell.name: Gift certificate for first music lessons
whatElseYouSell.pitchLine: "A printable gift certificate for a month of music lessons to tuck under a new guitar, sold online through December."
whatElseYouSell.when: Pitch in October, live by Thanksgiving.

whatElseYouSell.name: Music store counter cards
whatElseYouSell.pitchLine: "Cards for the local music store counter with a scan code to book a first lesson, handed to every family buying a beginner instrument."

whatElseYouSell.name: Monthly practice tips email for families
whatElseYouSell.pitchLine: "A short monthly email with a practice tip by instrument, recital dates and open slots, written and sent for the studio."
whatElseYouSell.when: Month 3, once the family list is clean.

withoutAI.pitchLine: "The music store where your students rent their first violin has no rental page. Introduce me and I'll build rentals and repairs online."
withoutAI.whyItWorks: Music stores depend on teacher referrals for rentals, so the studio owner's introduction is welcomed.

withoutAI.route: Piano tuners and instrument repair shops
withoutAI.whoPays: Each technician, at your normal rate
withoutAI.pitchLine: "The piano tuner you send families to needs an online booking page. Your recommendation does the selling."
withoutAI.whyItWorks: Tuners and repair techs live on referrals from teachers and rarely have a working site.

withoutAI.route: Local venues that host student shows
withoutAI.pitchLine: "The café or small venue that hosts your student band nights needs an events calendar and booking page. You can introduce me."
withoutAI.whyItWorks: Small venues fill quiet nights with student shows and trust the teacher who brings an audience.

withoutAI.pitchLine: "The church where your voice students sing needs a music ministry page with choir rehearsals and auditions. I'd like an introduction."
withoutAI.whyItWorks: Music teachers often play or direct at churches, and church sites are rarely kept current.

withoutAI.pitchLine: "The middle school band your students play in needs a booster page for fundraising, concert dates and volunteers. I'll build it."
withoutAI.whyItWorks: Boosters are parent-run and buy when a teacher they trust names someone.

withoutAI.route: Dance and theatre studios needing accompanists
withoutAI.whoPays: Each studio, at your normal rate
withoutAI.pitchLine: "The theatre studio that hires your pianist for musicals needs a class and audition page. Your teacher's introduction opens the door."
withoutAI.whyItWorks: Performing arts studios share families and staff, and owners trust each other's recommendations.

withAI.route: Rental and sizing assistant for the music store
withAI.pitchLine: "Parents ask which violin size fits their child or whether to rent or buy a keyboard, and the store's assistant answers and starts the rental."
withAI.whyItWorks: Sizing questions block rentals. Answering them at night turns into rental contracts.

withAI.route: Tuning booking assistant for piano technicians
withAI.pitchLine: "Homeowners ask when their piano was last tuned and book the next visit, and the technician's route fills without phone tag."
withAI.whyItWorks: Technicians are on the road all day and miss calls. One booked tuning a month pays for it.

withAI.route: Event and booking enquiries assistant for small venues
withAI.pitchLine: "Bands and teachers ask about open nights, sound gear and ticket splits, and the venue gets a hold request at any hour."
withAI.whyItWorks: Venue owners answer booking messages after closing. Each held date has value.

withAI.route: Choir rehearsal question line for churches
withAI.pitchLine: "Choir members ask what's on this week's rehearsal list and which robe colour, and get answers from the music director's notes."
withAI.whyItWorks: Volunteer choirs repeat the same questions weekly, and directors welcome a break.

withAI.route: Concert and fundraiser assistant for band boosters
withAI.pitchLine: "Band parents ask about call times, uniforms and the fundraiser deadline, and get answers from the booster packet."
withAI.whyItWorks: Booster officers are volunteers drowning in parent texts. One season of relief sells the renewal.

withAI.route: Audition sign-up assistant for theatre studios
withAI.pitchLine: "Families ask about audition songs, slots and callbacks for the next musical, and the studio's assistant answers and books an audition time."
withAI.whyItWorks: Audition weeks flood small studios. A booked slot is a clear result.

softwareAI.name: First-lesson follow-up and enrolment offer
softwareAI.pitchLine: "After a first music lesson, the parent gets a note from the teacher and a link to lock in the weekly slot before someone else takes it."
softwareAI.whenAndWhatItTakes: Day 30. Needs lesson rates and calendar access.

softwareAI.name: Weekly lesson calendar with teacher slots
softwareAI.pitchLine: "Each music teacher's weekly slots shown by instrument, with recurring lessons booked once for the whole term."
softwareAI.whenAndWhatItTakes: Month 2. Needs teacher availability and lesson lengths.

softwareAI.name: Make-up lesson scheduler
softwareAI.pitchLine: "A missed piano lesson becomes a credit the family books into an open slot, under the studio's make-up rule, with no texting back and forth."
softwareAI.whenAndWhatItTakes: Month 2, the first time make-ups become a headache. Needs the make-up policy.

softwareAI.name: Music school enquiry answerer
softwareAI.pitchLine: "'What age can she start violin' and 'do you have Tuesday guitar slots' get answered from the music school's own pages, with the first-lesson link."
softwareAI.whenAndWhatItTakes: Month 2. Needs instruments, teachers, rates and openings. Comes with the AI maintenance retainer.

softwareAI.name: Monthly tuition autopay
softwareAI.pitchLine: "Music lesson tuition charged monthly on the same day, with a polite note when a card fails, so the teacher never asks a parent for a cheque."
softwareAI.whenAndWhatItTakes: Month 2, if they still collect by cash or cheque. Needs rates and payment account.

softwareAI.name: Practice log for students
softwareAI.pitchLine: "Students log practice minutes and the pieces they worked on, and the teacher sees the week before the lesson starts."
softwareAI.whenAndWhatItTakes: Month 3. Needs teacher buy-in and the studio's practice expectations.

softwareAI.name: Lesson reminders and recital deadlines
softwareAI.pitchLine: "Families get a reminder before each music lesson, and recital piece and sign-up deadlines go out without the teacher chasing."
softwareAI.whenAndWhatItTakes: Month 2. Needs lesson calendar and the recital timeline.

softwareAI.name: Music studio phone answering
softwareAI.pitchLine: "While every teacher is mid-lesson, the music studio phone still gets answered, the instrument question handled and the first lesson booked."
softwareAI.whenAndWhatItTakes: Month 4, once they trust you. Needs rates, openings and booking access. Comes with the AI maintenance retainer.

softwareAI.name: Lesson note to parents
softwareAI.pitchLine: "The teacher says a few words after the lesson, and the parent gets a clear note on the piece, the practice goal and one thing to praise."
softwareAI.whenAndWhatItTakes: Month 3. Teacher approves every note. Comes with the AI maintenance retainer.

softwareAI.name: Review reply drafts for the music school
softwareAI.pitchLine: "Music lesson reviews get a short reply drafted in the studio owner's voice, mentioning the instrument and teacher, ready to approve between students."
softwareAI.whenAndWhatItTakes: Month 2, with the review asks. Comes with the AI maintenance retainer.

softwareAI.name: Recital programme builder
softwareAI.pitchLine: "Students submit their recital piece and composer, the running order builds itself by level, and the printed programme comes out spelled right."
softwareAI.whenAndWhatItTakes: Month 4, before the next recital. Needs the recital date and format.

softwareAI.name: Rehearsal room booking with door codes
softwareAI.pitchLine: "Bands book a rehearsal room by the hour, pay up front and get a door code for that slot, so the studio earns at night without staff."
softwareAI.whenAndWhatItTakes: Month 4, only for studios with rooms. Needs rates and the lock system.

softwareAI.name: Quitting-risk check-in
softwareAI.pitchLine: "A student who missed two music lessons in a row triggers a friendly note to the parent offering a new time or a different piece to reignite interest."
softwareAI.whenAndWhatItTakes: Month 4. Needs attendance from the lesson calendar.

softwareAI.name: Practice coach between lessons
softwareAI.pitchLine: "Students ask how to count a tricky rhythm or which scale to warm up with, and get the teacher's own guidance for their level, not internet advice."
softwareAI.whenAndWhatItTakes: Month 5. Needs teacher-written practice notes by level and approval of answers. Comes with the AI maintenance retainer.

softwareAI.name: Repertoire picker by level and style
softwareAI.pitchLine: "A teacher enters a student's level and favourite songs, and gets a shortlist of pieces from the studio's own library to choose from."
softwareAI.whenAndWhatItTakes: Month 5. Needs the studio's repertoire list with levels. Comes with the AI maintenance retainer.

softwareAI.name: Teacher pay report
softwareAI.pitchLine: "Each music teacher's lessons taught, make-ups and recital hours added up for payroll at the end of the month."
softwareAI.whenAndWhatItTakes: Month 5, for schools with several teachers. Needs pay rules.

softwareAI.name: Lapsed student welcome-back
softwareAI.pitchLine: "Students who stopped lessons over summer get a note in August with their old teacher's open times."
softwareAI.whenAndWhatItTakes: Month 6. Needs past student list.

softwareAI.name: Exam and audition prep tracker
softwareAI.pitchLine: "Required pieces, scales and theory for each student's graded exam or audition, ticked off by the teacher as they're ready."
softwareAI.whenAndWhatItTakes: Month 6, for studios preparing exam or audition students. Needs requirements per level.

softwareAI.name: Teacher-to-student match helper
softwareAI.pitchLine: "A new family describes the child's age, favourite music and personality, and the helper suggests the best-fit music teacher with open slots."
softwareAI.whenAndWhatItTakes: Month 6, for schools with several teachers. Needs teacher profiles and the owner's matching rules. Comes with the AI maintenance retainer.

softwareAI.name: Retention forecast by teacher
softwareAI.pitchLine: "The owner sees which teachers' students are likely to drop before summer, from attendance and practice logs, with a suggested check-in."
softwareAI.whenAndWhatItTakes: Month 8, after months of attendance data. Comes with the AI maintenance retainer.

routesToBiggerBuyer.route: Productise the first-lesson booking and practice log for private teachers
routesToBiggerBuyer.pitchLine: "I built a first-lesson booking and practice log for one music school. Every private piano teacher tracks the same things in a paper notebook."
routesToBiggerBuyer.whyItWorks: Private teachers are many and small, and they meet through teachers' associations and recital halls.

routesToBiggerBuyer.whoPays: The state or local music teachers association
routesToBiggerBuyer.pitchLine: "Offer every member teacher a studio page template with lesson booking and recital sign-up, as a membership benefit."
routesToBiggerBuyer.whyItWorks: Teacher associations need practical benefits and already run recitals and exams members care about.

routesToBiggerBuyer.route: Teacher finder for an instrument retailer chain
routesToBiggerBuyer.pitchLine: "Every beginner instrument you sell needs a teacher. A find-a-teacher page with local studios' booking links keeps families coming back for strings and books."
routesToBiggerBuyer.whyItWorks: Retailers want beginners to stick with it, and teachers drive repeat purchases.

routesToBiggerBuyer.pitchLine: "Franchise music schools lose families when a location's teacher list is out of date. A shared directory with live open slots per location fixes that across the network."
routesToBiggerBuyer.whyItWorks: One contract becomes every location, and franchisors roll out what works.

routesToBiggerBuyer.route: Agency licence for the music lesson template
routesToBiggerBuyer.pitchLine: "Your agency picks up music teachers it can't price low enough to build from scratch. License my template with the instrument chooser and booking built in."
routesToBiggerBuyer.whyItWorks: Agencies turn small music jobs away. A finished template makes them worth taking.

routesToBiggerBuyer.route: Youth orchestra and honour band registration
routesToBiggerBuyer.whoPays: The youth orchestra or honour band organisation, annually
routesToBiggerBuyer.pitchLine: "Your auditions, seating results, rehearsal schedule and tuition each season need one registration site. I build for the teachers who prepare your players."
routesToBiggerBuyer.whyItWorks: Youth orchestras run the same audition cycle every year, and private teachers are their feeder network.

routesToBiggerBuyer.route: Rock camp and summer music camp operators
routesToBiggerBuyer.pitchLine: "Your summer rock camp needs band placement by level, weekly sessions and a final-show page. I built the camp page for a music school already."
routesToBiggerBuyer.whyItWorks: Camp operators share students with music schools and buy on a hard spring deadline.

routesToBiggerBuyer.whoPays: The district or education foundation, annually
routesToBiggerBuyer.pitchLine: "Your after-school guitar and piano programmes run through outside teachers. A registration and roster page per school fills them."
routesToBiggerBuyer.whyItWorks: Districts contract music teachers already, and the client is a warm introduction.

routesToBiggerBuyer.whoPays: Each studio, at your normal rate
routesToBiggerBuyer.pitchLine: "Recording studios and rehearsal spaces need hourly booking with door codes, the same one I built for a music school's rooms."
routesToBiggerBuyer.whyItWorks: The booking pattern is built, and local musicians move between these places.

routesToBiggerBuyer.route: Senior centres' music and choir programmes
routesToBiggerBuyer.whoPays: The senior centre or community, annually
routesToBiggerBuyer.pitchLine: "Your residents' piano lessons and choir run with a visiting music teacher. A schedule and sign-up page families can see makes it an amenity."
routesToBiggerBuyer.whyItWorks: Senior communities market activities to families, and music teachers already visit.

routesToBiggerBuyer.whoPays: New music schools in other towns
routesToBiggerBuyer.pitchLine: "With one piano and guitar school in {City} booking first lessons online, I show studios in neighbouring towns the working example."
routesToBiggerBuyer.whyItWorks: Music schools rarely compete across towns, and a working example sells itself.

routesToBiggerBuyer.pitchLine: "You started setting up lesson scheduling software and still take bookings by text. I can finish it, having done it for another music school."
routesToBiggerBuyer.whyItWorks: Stuck owners already pay for the software and want it working before fall.

upsellLadder.offer: Music school site build plus care plan, one contract

upsellLadder.line: "The music school site and the care plan go on one contract, so a new teacher or rate is a text to me."

upsellLadder.trigger: First-lesson bookings start and a family doesn't commit to a weekly slot.
upsellLadder.line: "That family who loved the first guitar lesson but didn't book weekly would have heard from the teacher that night."

upsellLadder.trigger: They mention chasing late tuition or cheques.
upsellLadder.line: "Music lesson tuition can collect itself on the same day each month. No more asking parents at the door."

upsellLadder.offer: Review asks after a first recital
upsellLadder.trigger: The next recital date is set.
upsellLadder.line: "Recital parents are your proudest reviewers. Let's ask them the day after."

upsellLadder.trigger: They say make-up lesson requests are eating their evenings.
upsellLadder.line: "Make-up music lessons can book themselves into open slots under your rule."
"A practice log shows you the week before the lesson starts, and parents see it too."

upsellLadder.trigger: It's July or early December and teachers have open weekly slots.
upsellLadder.line: "Your teachers have open slots before the fall and holiday rush. Let's point ads at the first-lesson booking."

upsellLadder.offer: Introduction to the local music store
upsellLadder.trigger: They mention the store owner asking about the site or referring students.
upsellLadder.line: "The music store sends you beginners and has no rental page. Would you introduce me?"
